Disclosure  to  Promote  the  Right  To  Information 

Whereas  the  Parliament  of  India  has  set  out  to  provide  a  practical  regime  of  right  to 
information  for  citizens  to  secure  access  to  information  under  the  control  of  public  authorities, 
in  order  to  promote  transparency  and  accountability  in  the  working  of  every  public  authority, 
and  whereas  the  attached  publication  of  the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards  is  of  particular  interest 
to  the  public,  particularly  disadvantaged  communities  and  those  engaged  in  the  pursuit  of 
education  and  knowledge,  the  attached  public  safety  standard  is  made  available  to  promote  the 
timely  dissemination  of  this  information  in  an  accurate  manner  to  the  public.

IS  :  S323  •  1969 

Indian  Standard 

LETTER  SYMBOLS  AND  ABBREVIATIONS 
FOR  ELECTRON  TUBES 

0.    FOREWORD 

0.1  This  I/idian  Standard  was  adopted  by  the  Indian  Standards 
Institution  on  30  August  1969^  after  the  draft  finalized  by  tlie  Election 
Tubes  and  Valves  Sectional  Committee  had  been  approved  by  the  Elec- 
trotechnical  Division  CounciJ. 

0.2  This  standard  deals  with  the  letter  symbols  and  abbreviations  to 
be  used  for  electron  tubes  by  manufacturers  in  their  catalogues  and  in 
oth*^r  technical  literature.  The  mam  purpose  of  this  standard  is  to 
enable  the  technical  characteristics  of  the  manufacturers'  products  to  be 
described  to  their  customers^  and  it  is  in  this  field  that  the  standard 
is  expected  to  prove  rr.ost  useful. 

0-2il  A  system  of  letter  symbols  and  abb  rev]  at  ions  is  also  necessary 
for  mathematical  calculation  concerning  the  operation  of  election  tubes 
and  for  alhed  technical  descriptions. 

0.3  In  preparing  this  standard,  endeavour  has  been  made  to  unify  the 
syrnbols  pecuhar  to  the  electronic  tubf^  industry,  and  at  the  same  time  to 
ensure  that  they  do  rot  generally  conflict  v^ith  those  used  in  wider  fields 
of  electric  and  electronic  engineering,  Similarly,  every  effort  has  been 
made  to  ensure  that  as  far  as  possible  symbols  have  been  euiployed  which 
have  a  sifrnificancc  common  to  all  branches  of  engineering. 

0.4  It  is  hoped  that  by  means  of  this  standard  the  interests  of  those  who 
are  concerned  with  electron  tubes  WjII  be  best  served;  they  will  obtain 
the  advantages  of  accepted  common  symbols  and  at  the  same  time 
avoid  any  inconvenience  which  inlgtit  follow  the  adoption  of  specialized 
terms  and  symbols  in  conflict  with  those  more  generally  employed. 

C.5  It  is  recognized  that  the  symbols  and  abbreviations  included  in  this 
standard  are  not  exhaustive.  It  is  recommended  that,  as  such  needs 
arise,  symbols  and  abbreviations  should  be  chosen  that  they  do  not 
conflict  with  the  generalJy  accepted  symboJs  and  abbrevianons;  set  out 
in  this  standard.  In  this  way  new  symbols  and  abbreviations  consistent 
with  this  scheme,  may  achieve  that  general  acceptance  which  is  a  sound 
prelude  to  standardization. 


IS  :  5323  -  1969 

0,6  Tn  choosing  the  symbols  and  abbreviations,  the  convenience  of  their 
production  with  standard  printer's  type  as  weJl  aa  on  a  typewriter  haa 
been  borne  in  mind. 

0.7  This  standard  is  largely  b^ged  on  B  S.  1409:1050  *  Letter  symbols  for 
electronic  vaivea*  issued  by  ihe  British  Standards  rnstiiution,  and  it  also 
cakes  into  acrount  the  practice  followed  in  this  country.  Attempts  have 
also  been  made  to  bring  about  viniforniity  as  far  as  practicable  with 
symbols  adopted  for  semiconrinctor  devices  (  IS  '  3715-1966*  ). 

0*8  This  document  rovers  general  symbols  for  receiving  tubes,  transmitting 
and  industrial  lubes  and  cathode-ray  tubes.  Additional  symbols  for 
covering  specific  characteristics  for  dilTcrent  types  of  tubes  are  not  covered 
at  present  and  may  be  included  cither  in  the  form  of  an  aTnendment  or 
future  revision  oF  this  standard.  Symbols  for  micro-wave  tubes  are 
also  not  coveied  by  this  standard. 

0.9  This  standard  is  one  of  a  series  of  Indian  Standards  on  electron 
tubes. 


\.  SCOPE 

1*1  This   standard    covers   the   letter   symbols  and  abbrevations  used  in 
connection  with  electron  tubes. 

2.  GENERAL  ASPECTS 

2*1  Q^nantity  Symbols  —  With  the  exception   of  symbols    for    voltage 
and  current  J  the  following  general  rules  have  been  adopted; 

a)  Symbols  relating  to  a  tube  itself  are  denoted  by   letters   in   small 
type  (  prititer's  Mower  ca^e');  and 

b)  Symbols   relating    to    associated    circuitry    are  denoted  by  lelters 
in  capital  type. 

2-1.1  Values  of  voltage  or  current  are  denoted  by  letter  symbols  in 
capital  type  except  that  mstamantoua  values  are  denoted  by  letter 
symhola  in  small  type. 

ExampUs: 

DC  value  of  voltage  Tdc 

RMS  value  of  voltage  t'nn* 


*I.etter  syrtiboJa  for  semiconductor  device^ 


IS  :  5323  -  1969 

Average  value  of  voltage  Kav 

Inatamaneous  value  of  voltage  v 

2.2  Subacript  Symbols  —  Any  finalificaiion  of  n  symbol  i?  e(Tccled  by 
means  of  a  subscript  and,  where  the  subscript  jiself  is  quahfiedj  this  is 
indicated  by  a  leltci  or  figure  in  the  ^anio  Hnr;  a^  the  Mib-^crjpt. 

ExamplfS'. 

First  grid  §\ 

Voltage  on  first  grid  P^gi 

NftTH  —  Where   no   confusion   iji   likirly    to    recall,   qualifying   symbols    ihcwn    as 
subscripts^  may  bt  in  line  wiih  the  main  symbol  for  typewrictRn  flocumenta. 
ExartipU:  Vg^ 

2.2.1  When  the  subscript  consists  of  two  groups  of  symbols  representing 
the  terminal  points  between  which  a  measurement  is  made  the  two  groups 
need  not  normally  be  sf^paraled.  If  ronfuaion  is  likely  lo  occur  the  two 
groups  may  be  separated  by  a  comma. 

Examples'. 

Capacitance  between  anode  and  first  grid  Cb,^! 

Insulation  resistance  between  anode  and  cathode      ran

second  may  be  In  brackets,

or  can,  partly  or  wholly  covering  the  tube  envelope  )

3.2  Rules  for  Application  of  Electrode  Symbols 

3.2.1  To  distinguish  between  electrodes  of  the  same  typft  the  following 
rules  shall  apply 

a)  Subscripts  need  not  be  added  iT  confusion  is  not  likely  to  ari.'ie; 

b)  f  ti  multiple  unit  tubes  (  such  as  a.  triode-peniode  )  the  respective 
electrodes  may  be  distinguished  by  adding  one  of  the  followipg 
letters  in  capital  letter  as  a  subscript: 

Triode  T 

Tetrode  Q 

Pentode  P 

Hexode,  heptode,  etc  H 

Rectifier  R 

Detection  dioJe  D 

Examples  codgritig  one  section  nf  a  muliipU  tube  and  two  or   more   seettons   of 
a  muUipU  Otbe: 

Capacitance  between  triode  gride  and  triode  heater  Cgrb 

Capacitance  between  triode  grid  and  hexode  grid  CgraH 

3.2.2  Where  there  arc  twu  or  more  9imila.r  electrode  systems  which 
caiinat  be  distinguished  according  to  the  type  of  tube  or  function,  a 
printer's  ^primc'  or  'primes'  or  in  the  case  of  lypewriling  an  apostrophe 
or  apostrophes,  shall  be  addeo;  one  for  the  first  electrode  system,  two  for 
the  second  electrode  system  and  so  on. 

ExampU: 

Anode  voltage  on  the  first  section  of  detection  diode  Vb'd 


IS  t  5323  -  1969 

3.2.3  If  more  than  one  grid  is  present,  /brming  part  of  the  same 
section  of  the  tube,  the  grids  shall  be  distinguished  by  adding  a  figure 
as  a  subscript,  the  figure  showing  the  sequence  of  grids  counting  from 
the  cathode.     A  simiJar  convention  shall  apply  to  a  sequence  of  anodes. 

3.2.4  Two  or  more  internal  shields  or  switch  contacts  (  either  moving 
or  fixed  )  shaJI  be  distinguished  by  adding  a  tigure  as  a  subscript. 

3.2.5  Secondary-emission  electrodes  shall  be  considered  as  cathodes. 
The  primaiy  cathode  shall  be  denoted  by  Al  and  the  secondary  cathodes 
by  k2,  A:3,  etc. 

3.2.6  Where  necessary,  the  polarity  of  the  filament  shall  be  indicated 
thus: 

/{  +  }*    /(  -  ) 

3*2.7  Tappings  on  filament*  or  heaters  shall  be  indicated  by  the  use 
of  the  sufhx  'tap'.
